clue.text: Protest ? It's just one of those things

definitions.meaning: to protest or raise a complaint

definitions.text: It's just one of those things
definitions.meaning: simply a thing, any item at all

explanation.surface: A shrug of resignation after a complaint gets nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to raise an objection; as a noun it means a material item, one of the things around us.

clue.text: Book about the Curse of the Crafty Retainer

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other here

parts.note: taken as written
an oath is a curse or swear word

explanation.surface: A book about a sly servant's curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts OATH inside BOOK. The definition puns on 'craft' as a boat and 'retainer' as something that holds on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pole with a hook for holding on to a boat: it retains a craft.

clue.text: Topsy's friend has broken a lute — put a figure on it

parts.note: Topsy's friend in Uncle Tom's Cabin is little Eva

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl's friend smashes a musical instrument, and someone must price the damage.
explanation.walkthrough: Topsy and Eva are children in Harriet Beecher Stowe's Uncle Tom's Cabin. 'broken' scrambles A and LUTE into LUATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess the worth of something is to give it a number or price.

clue.text: No stopping for such a one

definitions.text: No stopping for such a one

parts.words: No stopping for such a one
parts.note: a stopping is a dental filling, and someone with no teeth needs none

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stopping' is an old word for a dental filling, not a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A person without teeth has nothing for a dentist to fill.

clue.text: Quixotic giant

parts.note: Don Quixote tilted at sails on the plain, believing them to be giants

explanation.walkthrough: In Cervantes' novel Don Quixote charges at a row of these, convinced they are giants waving their arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The deluded knight mistook these sail-driven mills for monsters, so each is a giant only in his imagination.

clue.text: It's swinging in the rain

parts.note: a car's blade swings to and fro across the glass when it rains, echoing the song 'Singin' in the Rain'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'Singin' in the Rain'; the thing swinging is a car's blade clearing the glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's rubber blade sweeps back and forth over the front glass in wet weather.

clue.text: Firmly determined to see the late Egyptian god

parts.note: the late describes someone dead
Set is the Egyptian god of storms and chaos

explanation.surface: Resolved to visit an ancient Egyptian deity who has died.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone utterly resolved on a course is fixed on it, an idiom.

clue.text: The heathen in his blindness

parts.note: from the hymn 'From Greenland's Icy Mountains': the heathen in his blindness bows down to wood and stone

explanation.walkthrough: Bishop Heber's hymn says the heathen in his blindness bows down to wood and stone, that is, worships graven images.
explanation.definitionFit: One who bows to images of wood and stone worships false gods.

clue.text: Mrs. McGurgle invited to step ashore ?

definitions.meaning: Mrs McGurgle is the seaside boarding-house keeper in P. G. Wodehouse's stories
read as '...!', an invitation for a woman to come ashore

explanation.surface: A woman is asked to leave the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as 'land, lady' and it is a command to a woman to come ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wodehouse character runs lodgings, and the split phrase bids a woman disembark.

clue.text: Tea-time delicacy, about a cent this …

indicators.note: about means going round, so the colour word wraps around the cent and the article

parts.note: this points ahead to the answer of the next clue, the brownish crimson shade

explanation.surface: A cake for tea priced at around a cent.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots tie this clue to the next: 'this' stands for the 10-across answer, which goes 'about' C (cent) and A.
explanation.definitionFit: This almond biscuit is a classic sweet treat served with afternoon tea.

clue.text: … brownish crimson banger

definitions.meaning: a loud firework or distress rocket that goes off with a bang

explanation.surface: A dark red firework continues the previous clue's thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banger' here is not a sausage but an exploding firework, the sense used of a signal rocket.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a deep red-brown hue and also an explosive signal firework.

clue.text: The pennyworth that proved Cartesian existence

definitions.text: The pennyworth that proved Cartesian existence

parts.words: The pennyworth that proved Cartesian existence
parts.note: a penny is offered for what you are thinking, and Descartes said 'I think, therefore I am'

explanation.walkthrough: Two references meet: the saying 'a penny for them' and Descartes' cogito, which proved his existence from the fact that he was thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas in the mind are what one offers a penny for, and Descartes rested his proof of existence on having them.

clue.text: Attack is alas confounded

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cry of dismay at an assault going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' scrambles IS and ALAS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To assault someone is to set upon them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: For the impractical the alternative is to lose nothing

parts.note: or is the word that introduces an alternative

indicators.note: to lose means to give up something, so the word to drops a letter

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Advice that the unrealistic person's only option is to give up nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose nothing' takes O from TO, leaving T. 'For' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone concerned with ideas rather than practice is the stereotype of an unworldly thinker.

clue.text: Bristol's fashionable line?

parts.note: the saying '... and Bristol fashion' means neat and in good order

explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'shipshape and Bristol fashion' comes from the port of Bristol, where ships had to be kept well stowed; 'line' looks like a fashion range.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase that goes with 'Bristol fashion' means tidy and orderly, as a well-kept vessel is.

clue.text: Hound of heaven? Well, terrier

parts.note: a dog whose name sounds like the heavens is in fact a breed of terrier named after a Scottish island

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'Hound of Heaven' is a famous poem, but the setter means a dog whose name sounds like the sky: a Scottish terrier breed named after an island of the Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-haired terrier breed takes its name from the Hebridean island, whose name sounds like the heavens.

clue.text: Dance of a horse in the sand

indicators.note: in means one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A horse prancing on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ARAB inside SAND. 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately Spanish court dance in triple time, a type of dance.

clue.text: It's otherwise than gay, a sword of Islam

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so these letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: A curved blade described as anything but cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges THAN GAY A. 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turkish curved sabre without a guard, a weapon of the Ottoman world.

clue.text: Beg that the victim be heard .

indicators.note: be heard means the word is spoken aloud and a soundalike is written

parts.note: prey is the victim of a hunter

explanation.surface: A plea that the person who suffered should be given a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be heard' turns PREY (the victim) into a word of the same sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat or implore is to plead, a direct synonym.

clue.text: The man in the Roman street

definitions.text: The man in the Roman street

parts.words: The man in the Roman street
parts.note: the 'man in the street' is an ordinary person, and in Rome that meant a commoner

explanation.walkthrough: A twist on 'the man in the street': the common people of ancient Rome were the plebs.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinary citizen of ancient Rome belonged to the commoners rather than the patrician class.

clue.text: Eumenides as once featured on — T.V.

definitions.text: Eumenides as once featured on — T.V.

parts.words: Eumenides as once featured on — T.V.
parts.note: the Eumenides are the Furies who pursue wrongdoers, and the same name was a 1960s television spy series

explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the Eumenides, or Furies, punish crimes; the same word titled a British TV series with Steed and Mrs Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Furies take vengeance on wrongdoers, and the word was also the name of the 1960s spy show.

clue.text: Slip round the ice backwards-that's out of the ordinary

indicators.note: backwards means the whole combination is read from right to left
round means one word goes about the other

parts.note: a lapse is a slip or small error

explanation.surface: Someone falls on the ice going backwards, which is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts ICE inside LAPSE to give LAICEPSE, and 'backwards' turns that whole run around.
explanation.definitionFit: Special or exceptional, a slightly old-fashioned synonym for something notable.

clue.text: Conundrums in games perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests a possible other form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Puzzles that may turn up during games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges IN and GAMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddles and puzzles are mysteries to be solved.

clue.text: Two bills one article of Australian wattle

indicators.note: two means the following piece appears twice in a row

parts.note: ac is short for account, which is a bill
one is the Roman numeral I
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Paying a couple of invoices for an Australian plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two' doubles AC. Wattle is the Australian name for these trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden wattle is a species of this tree genus, and the name covers them in Australia.

clue.text: One of 11 that's merry, if a bit chicken

definitions.meaning: with 'merry' in front, the answer to clue 11 in the singular names the forked bone of a bird
a forked bone from a chicken, pulled by two people making a wish

explanation.surface: A cheerful idea, though slightly cowardly.
explanation.walkthrough: Merrythought is an old name for the forked bone of a bird's breast; put 'merry' before one of 11-across's answer and you have it.
explanation.definitionFit: The forked clavicle of a fowl is a piece of the bird, also called a merrythought.

clue.text: The "in" style of entertainment

parts.note: being in means being at your own house, and a party held in someone's house is a style of entertaining

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like fashionable, but it means not out of the house; the phrase is also a reception held at one's home.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means being in one's house, and as a noun names a reception held there.

clue.text: He thanked God he was not as other men

definitions.text: He thanked God he was not as other men

parts.words: He thanked God he was not as other men
parts.note: a quotation from the parable in Luke 18 of the self-righteous man praying in the temple beside the tax collector

explanation.walkthrough: In the Gospel of Luke a self-righteous man prays 'God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are'.
explanation.definitionFit: The parable's proud worshipper was a member of the strict Jewish sect, and the word now means a self-righteous hypocrite.

clue.text: This creature is around, unfortunately, no longer

definitions.text: This creature is around, unfortunately, no longer

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lament that a certain animal has died out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' scrambles IS and AROUND; read as a whole, the clue describes an extinct creature.
explanation.definitionFit: These prehistoric reptiles are extinct, so they are no longer around.

clue.text: Most ' severe he would be, if canonized

indicators.note: canonizing a man adds the saint's abbreviation before his name, so the word for most severe loses it

parts.note: the sternest person is the most severe

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain man would be the harshest of all if made a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: St is short for Saint: prefix it to a man's first name and you get the word meaning most severe.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a man's first name, so it can stand for 'he'.
